parts.t: Second and Third Schedules: salaries and oaths
items: **Second Schedule:** Emoluments, allowances, and privileges of constitutional office-holders (President, Governors, Presiding Officers, SC/HC Judges, CAG).
**Trap Pair:** Second Schedule = Salaries ↔ Third Schedule = Forms of Oaths.

**Third Schedule Exclusions:** The forms of oath for the President (Art. 60), Vice-President (Art. 69), and Governor (Art. 159) are codified directly in their respective constitutional articles—they are NOT contained in the Third Schedule.

**Determining Authority vs. Source Fund:** Who determines the salary (Parliament/State Legislature by law) is a distinct legal question from which fund pays it (Consolidated Fund of India vs. State) and whether it is Charged or Voted.

lectures.title: Citizenship: Part II and the Citizenship Act, 1955

items: **Constitutional Framework:** Governed under Part II (Articles 5–11); primarily identified citizenship at the commencement of the Constitution (26 January 1950).

**Exclusive Legislative Authority (Art. 11):** Parliament has the exclusive constitutional power to regulate citizenship, acquisition, and termination by law (Enacted the Citizenship Act, 1955; Citizenship Rules under Section 18).
**Trap:** State Legislatures, the President, or the Election Commission have no power to make citizenship laws.

**Single Citizenship & Single Domicile:** India provides for a Single Citizenship and a single domicile across the entire territory (a unitary feature of the federal structure; unlike the USA which has dual federal and state citizenship).
Citizenship at the commencement of the Constitution
Domicile in India + born in India / either parent born / resident for ≥ 5 yrs prior to 1950

Parliament to regulate citizenship by law

**1. Renunciation:** Voluntary surrender of citizenship by an Indian national.
**2. Termination:** Automatic loss when an Indian citizen voluntarily acquires the citizenship of another country (Art. 9).

**3. Deprivation (Sec. 10):** Compulsory termination by the Central Government on grounds of fraud, disloyalty to the Constitution, unlawful trading with an enemy during war, or imprisonment for ≥ 2 years within 5 years of naturalization/registration.

**Head of State / Presidential Eligibility Trap:** In the USA, only a natural-born citizen can become President; In India, both a citizen by birth AND a naturalized citizen are eligible to become President of India (Art. 58).
**What Does NOT Acquire Citizenship:** Depositing money in Indian banks / purchasing property in India - NO.
**What Does NOT Cause Automatic Loss:** Marrying a foreign citizen - NO (Does not by itself revoke citizenship).
**What Does NOT Cause Automatic Loss:** Criticizing the government or policies - NO.
**Deprivation of Naturalized Citizens:** Statement claiming "A naturalized citizen can never be deprived of citizenship" - FALSE (Can be deprived under Section 10).

parts.t: National Emergency: legislative and financial mechanisms
items: **Term Extension of Legislatures:** Lok Sabha & State Assemblies: Parliament can extend their terms by law for 1 year at a time, up to a maximum of 6 months after the Emergency ceases.
**Laws on State List Subjects:** Parliament acquires overriding legislative jurisdiction over State List subjects; such laws cease to operate 6 months after the Emergency is revoked.

**Modifying Revenue Distribution (Art. 354):** The President is empowered to modify the constitutional distribution of revenues between the Union and States (valid up to the end of the financial year in which the proclamation ceases).

Operates on both External Emergency AND Internal Emergency (Armed Rebellion)

Does not operate during an "Armed Rebellion" proclamation
Articles 20 & 21 CANNOT be suspended under any circumstances (44th CAA)

parts.t: President's Rule (Art. 356) and extension beyond 1 year
items: **Invocation Basis:** Imposed when the government of a State cannot be carried on in accordance with the provisions of the Constitution; the President may act on a report from the Governor OR suo motu (otherwise).

**Conditions for Extension Beyond 1 Year (Up to 3-Year Cap):** 1. A National Emergency is in operation in the whole of India or in any part of the State, AND 2. The Election Commission of India certifies that general elections to the State Assembly cannot be held.
**Armed Rebellion:** Replaced "Internal Disturbance" with "Armed Rebellion" under Article 352.
**Approval time:** Reduced parliamentary approval time for National Emergency from 2 months to 1 month.
**Articles 20 and 21:** Guaranteed that the enforcement of Articles 20 and 21 can NEVER be suspended under Article 359.
**Written advice:** Added requirement that the President can proclaim National Emergency only upon written advice of the Union Cabinet.
**1975 Emergency Timeline:** Proclaimed on 25 June 1975 (on ground of Internal Disturbance) and formally withdrawn on 21 March 1977.

parts.t: Article 371 series: pairs not to confuse
items: **371 vs 371-A:** Art. 371 applies to Maharashtra & Gujarat, whereas Art. 371-A applies to Nagaland (Do not confuse 371 with 371-A).
**371-A vs 371-B vs 371-C (North-East Trap):** 371-A = Nagaland; 371-B = Assam; 371-C = Manipur.
**371-D vs 371-E (Andhra Trap):** 371-D = Andhra Pradesh & Telangana (Public employment / education quota); 371-E = Andhra Pradesh ONLY (Central University).
**371-J (98th CAA, 2012):** Specifically targets the socio-economic development of the Hyderabad–Karnataka region (6 backward districts).

parts.t: Scheduled Areas under the Fifth Schedule
items: **Constitutional Framework:** Governed under Part X (Article 244(1)) and the Fifth Schedule for the administration and control of Scheduled Areas and Scheduled Tribes.
**Declaring Authority:** The President of India declares and notifies an area as a Scheduled Area.
**Scope of State Executive Power:** Declaration of a Scheduled Area does NOT make it a Union Territory, create a separate state, or terminate the State Government's executive power.
**State executive power:** State executive power continues to extend over Scheduled Areas subject to the Fifth Schedule.

parts.t: Institutional governance and the Governor's special powers
items: **Tribal Advisory Council (TAC):** Mandatory advisory body established in each State having Scheduled Areas (under Paragraph 4 of the Fifth Schedule) to advise on matters pertaining to the welfare and advancement of Scheduled Tribes.
**Governor's Annual Report:** The Governor submits a report regarding the administration of Scheduled Areas directly to the President of India (annually or whenever required by the President).
**Trap:** It is submitted by the Governor to the President, NOT by the Chief Minister to the Union Home Ministry.
**Protection of Tribal Land (Paragraph 5):** The Governor is empowered to make regulations prohibiting or restricting the transfer of tribal land to non-tribals and regulating money-lending to STs.

**Samatha v. State of Andhra Pradesh (1997) Landmark Ruling:** The Supreme Court held that the transfer/lease of tribal land in Scheduled Areas to private parties for mining operations is null, void, and inoperative under the Fifth Schedule.

**North-East States Trap (AMTM):** The Sixth Schedule applies ONLY to Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, and Mizoram. It does NOT apply to Manipur or Nagaland.
**Declaring vs Reporting Authority:** Area Notification -- President; Administrative Report Submission -- Governor → President.
**Fifth vs Sixth Terminology:** Fifth Schedule = Scheduled Areas; Sixth Schedule = Tribal Areas.

lectures.title: Elections, anti-defection, ages and tenures, commissions and cases

items: **First-Past-the-Post (FPTP):** Plurality voting system where the candidate securing the highest number of valid votes is declared elected (absolute majority >50% not required).
**FPTP Rule:** Winning candidate requires only the highest vote count among contestants, not an absolute majority (50% + 1).

**Proportional Representation by Single Transferable Vote (PR-STV):** Multi-preference quota-based indirect voting system used for President, Vice-President, Rajya Sabha, and Legislative Councils to ensure proportional representation.
**Delimitation:** The statutory process of redrawing territorial constituency boundaries based on recent census figures to enforce equal representation.
**Right to Vote:** It is a Legal/Statutory Right, not a Fundamental Right.
**Representation of the People Act, 1950:** Framework for seat allocation, electoral rolls, and Legislative Council composition (Sec. 10 / Sched. 3 / Art. 171).

**Representation of the People Act, 1951:** Registration of political parties by ECI; conduct of elections; disqualification upon conviction (≥ 2 years imprisonment disqualified during term + 6 years post-release).

**Abhiram Singh v. C.D. Commachen (2017)** (Communalism & Secularism): Expanded Section 123(3) of RPA 1951; appeals to religion, race, caste, community, or language during election campaigns constitute a corrupt practice.
Member of Lok Sabha / State Legislative Assembly
Member of Rajya Sabha / State Legislative Council
**18 Years (Article 326):** Reduced from 21 to 18 years via the 61st CAA, 1988 (effective 1989).

**The 18 vs 21 Voting vs Contesting Trap:** 18 Years: Right to vote under Universal Adult Franchise (Art. 326); 21 Years: Minimum age to contest Panchayat / Municipality elections (Arts. 243F / 243V).
**5 Years:** President, Lok Sabha, State Legislative Assembly, Panchayats, Municipalities.
**6 Years:** Rajya Sabha members, State Legislative Council members (1/3rd retiring every 2 years).
**Constitutional Recognition:** Parties were NOT part of the original 1950 text; introduced via 52nd CAA, 1985 (10th Schedule).
**Scope of Disqualification:** Applies to members voluntarily giving up party membership or voting/abstaining contrary to party whips without prior permission.
**Merger Protection Exception:** Disqualification on grounds of defection does not apply if a party merges with another and ≥ 2/3rd of the members of the legislative party agree to the merger.
**Split exemption:** The original 1/3rd "split" exemption was omitted by the 91st CAA, 2003.
**Merger Fraction Trap:** Protection from defection requires agreement of 2/3rd members, NOT 1/3rd (1/3rd is the obsolete split threshold).
